why_it_is_not_the_strip: Columns 1 and 2 are pixel-identical to the ref in BOTH tests; a wrong offset or a wrong C/H would move them too.

In balancing-003 Android still paints exactly 85 aqua rows in columns 1-2 (y91-175), i.e. it balanced to H=ceil(C/3)=85, which requires C in [253,255] — the ref's 255. A strip 5px short would have given C=250 and H=84, one row shorter in EVERY column.
The shift equals the band's own width in both tests (3 and 5) — a strip error would be band-width independent.

The pure plan is pinned exact: MulticolFloatStripTest FS-C2/FS-C4 (offsets [0,10,250], C 253/255, H 100/85) and, new this wave, MulticolFloatStripRefRowsTest converts the plan into capture rows and asserts 161-163 / 171-175 against the frozen ref.

actual_mechanism.shape: .clear { clear:left; height:0 } > .bar { border-bottom: <w> solid orange } — the band is on a NESTED child of a zero-height box
actual_mechanism.step_1: runtimes/compose/src/main/java/com/styleconverter/runtime/sizing/SizingApplier.kt, the `is LengthValue.Exact -> m.height(v.px.toFloat().dp)` arm: Modifier.height(0.dp) hands the content FIXED 0 constraints, so `.bar` measures 0 tall instead of its CSS border-box 3px/5px (css-overflow-3 §2: `overflow: visible` content is not clamped by its box).
actual_mechanism.step_2: runtimes/compose/src/main/java/com/styleconverter/runtime/borders/sides/BorderSideApplier.kt, the `Side.BOTTOM -> Offset(0f, size.height - inset)` arm (inset = width/2): at size.height == 0 the stroke is centred on -w/2, i.e. the half-open band [-w, 0) — w px ABOVE the box. w=3 and w=5 reproduce the measured -3 and -5 exactly.
actual_mechanism.why_ios_is_exact: SwiftUI's .frame(height:) positions/clips but does not shrink the child's own measured size, so the twin keeps the 3pt/5pt bar and draws it at [0,w).

proposed_repair: A declared height must not clamp an overflowing child: apply the Compose height with a `wrapContentHeight(Alignment.Top, unbounded = true)` (or equivalent) so the content measures at its own block-size and overflows visibly, then re-measure the whole fixture net. Blast radius is EVERY explicit-height box in the Compose runtime, so this is a measured before/after with a device gate, not a drive-by — which is exactly why lane B6 did not take it. A narrower alternative, also needing the gate: make BorderSideApplier refuse to draw a side band outside the box (clamp `size.height - inset` at `inset`), which fixes the paint position but leaves the box 3-5px short.
